_comment: Geometry of the reference apartment building, taken from the author's drawing set (src/drawings/, DXF) (typical-floor plan, apartment plan and south elevation; clear room sizes as dimensioned there). Two mirror-image apartments per floor (A west, B east) around a common stair and lobby. Each space is one or more rectangles [x0,y0,x1,y1] in metres on WALL CENTRELINES (exterior walls 0.30 m, party and stair walls 0.25 m, partitions 0.15 m; outer footprint 19.15 m x 28.00 m, so the centreline outline runs from 0.15 to 19.00 m and from 0.15 to 27.85 m); apartment A and the core are listed, B is mirrored about mirror_x. The top of the plan faces north (+y); the main entrance and the stair face south. The west balcony (1.50 m clear) is enclosed by the exterior wall and modelled as an unconditioned zone. Areas, shared walls, exterior faces and orientations are DERIVED from the rectangles. cond = own split unit (none in the baths, maid room, lobby, corridor and hall); ton from the product catalogue by rated coverage (1.5 t 16-18 m2, 2 t 19-22 m2, 2.5 t 22-30 m2, 3 t 30-36 m2) of the clear area. clear_m = clear size on the drawing. gain_factor scales the per-area internal gain. Each space is coupled to the same space on the floor above through the slab. Each apartment has its own meter; the stair is on a common meter. windows_m = window widths per orientation (apartment A; W and E swap for B), height window_height_m.

representative_apartment._note: first floor above ground: neither ground-contact nor roof-exposed (typical intermediate apartment)

plan._note: Author's drawing set (src/drawings/: make_dxf.py, make_dxf_single.py, make_building.py -> DXF): 19.15 x 28.00 m outside; floor-to-floor 3.40 m (0.10 finish + 0.30 slab + 3.00 clear); windows sill +0.90, head +2.40; the west balcony is enclosed by the exterior wall (4.00 m window) and is modelled as an unconditioned zone.

3.0._note: 3 ton, 220 V, rotary (fixed-speed) compressor, cooling and heating, fan speeds low/mid/high (catalogue entry supplied by the author); modelled as an on/off unit that runs at full capacity whenever it runs
